summary.text: A tornado, or twister, is a rapidly rotating column of air reaching from the ground to the base of a cumulonimbus or cumulus cloud.
It usually becomes visible because the intense low pressure and fast spin make water vapour condense into a funnel cloud, though rain or dust can hide it completely.
Tornadoes are rated by the damage they cause, from EF0, which harms trees but not sturdy buildings, to EF5, which rips buildings off their foundations.

items.prompt: A spinning funnel hangs from a storm cloud but has not touched the ground. Is it a tornado yet?

options.label: Yes, any rotating funnel counts
Yes, if the winds are fast enough
No, it only counts if it hits buildings
No, it must touch both ground and cloud

items.explain: To count as a tornado, a vortex must be in contact with both the ground and the cloud base.

items.prompt: Survey teams arrive after a tornado. No one measured its winds. How will they most likely give it a Fujita rating?

options.label: By how long it lasted
By the damage it caused
By the colour of the funnel
By how many people saw it

items.explain: The Fujita and Enhanced Fujita scales rate tornadoes by the damage caused.

items.prompt: Your neighbour calls a tornado "a cyclone". In meteorology, why is that wrong?

options.label: A cyclone is a large system around low pressure
A cyclone spins only over the ocean
A cyclone has a much narrower funnel
A cyclone never brings any rain

items.explain: In meteorology a cyclone is a large weather system rotating around a centre of low pressure, and cyclones do not feature funnel clouds.

items.prompt: Why are tornadoes wrapped in heavy rain especially dangerous?

options.label: Rain makes their winds much faster
Rain turns them into waterspouts
Even experts may not be able to see them
Rain makes them last for several days

items.explain: Tornadoes can be fully hidden by rain or dust, so even experienced meteorologists might not see them.

items.prompt: A funnel is still high above a field, with no debris yet. A farmer assumes the ground is safe for now. What is the risk?

options.label: None until the funnel visibly touches down
Strong surface winds may already be blowing
Only hail, since funnels never bring wind
Only rain, since the funnel is still forming

items.explain: Most tornadoes produce strong surface winds while the visible funnel is still above the ground.

items.prompt: A single thunderstorm drops three separate tornadoes over an afternoon. What do forecasters call that group?

options.label: A tornado outbreak sequence
A derecho
A multiple-vortex tornado
A tornado family

items.explain: Multiple tornadoes produced by the same storm cell are called a tornado family.
